newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Enami starts up expanded copper refinery.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Enami starts up expanded copper refinery.

text.p: Chile's state mining company Empresa Nacional de Mineria (Enami) has started production at its expanded Ventanas copper refinery, said Jose Luis Figueroa, the manager in charge of the expansion project.
"We began startup at the new plant on October 20," Figueroa told Reuters. "It is now working practically at full speed."
The expansion, which cost $34 million, boosted the plant's processing capacity to more than 300,000 tonnes of fine copper a year from 200,000 tonnes, he said.

Ventanas, which lies on Chile's central coast, has signed long-term contracts to fill the extra capacity with state copper company Codelco's El Teniente division and Exxon Mineral's Chagres copper smelter, he said.
The refinery will process 80,000 tonnes a year of copper anodes from El Teniente's Caletones smelter and 30,000 tonnes of blister from Chagres, said Figueroa.
The refinery also processes all the production from Ventanas' own smelter and Enami's much smaller Paipote smelter which lies further north in the Third Region.
